title: Crewmate CPR in microgravity
whenToUse: Unresponsive crewmate who is not breathing normally or is only gasping.

steps.text: Start chest compressions right away, even without a defibrillator.
Wrap your legs around their chest. Lock your ankles behind their back.
steps.detail: Start immediately with the Evetts-Russomano method; if it does not work, switch to the reverse bear hug.

steps.text: Push hard and fast in the centre of the chest at 100 to 120 per minute with full recoil.
steps.detail: Microgravity methods do not reliably reach full Earth compression depth; push hard and fast continuously (or 30:2 if trained and willing). Switch to Handstand CPR once strapped to the CMRS restraint.
steps.caution: Do not wait for Earth or delay compressions.

steps.text: Defibrillate only when they are restrained on an electrically isolated surface.
steps.detail: Apply AED pads per diagrams once strapped to the CMRS. Use airway devices only with at least two rescuers and the patient restrained (second-generation supraglottic airway if nobody can intubate).
steps.caution: Clear everyone before AED rhythm analysis or shock, then resume CPR immediately.

redFlags: No return of normal breathing or movement.
Multiple AED shocks delivered or repeated arrest.
Suspected toxic air, electrocution or severe trauma.

escalation.text: Red flag or getting worse? Alert a crewmate now. Do not wait for Earth.
